analyst_view.overall: Early view: Manchester City are 7th with 9 points but in a poor run, losing three Premier League games in a row (the latest 3-1 at Nottingham Forest) and needing an Erling Haaland winner to beat Leipzig 3-2; Enzo Maresca has defended Gianluigi Donnarumma after his errors. Napoli (27th, 3 points) are in worse shape: beaten 4-1 at Porto and 2-0 at Juventus, and centre-back Rafa Marin is banned after his red card in Porto (ban not yet served).

goals.text: The numbers say 3.7 goals and I stay close to it. City are leaking goals (three conceded to Forest, two to Leipzig) and Napoli have conceded six in their last two games, so both defences are fragile. City's attack leans heavily on Haaland, which is the only thing keeping me from leaning higher.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. City will have the ball, but pundits have called them predictable and lacking dominance lately, and much of their threat comes through Haaland in the box rather than sustained wide pressure. I see no reason to move the figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards and I lean higher. Napoli collected four yellows and a red in Porto and finished with ten men at Juventus too, so discipline is an issue for Massimiliano Allegri's side. City also had two late bookings in Leipzig.

shots.text: The numbers say 29 shots. City usually take a lot of shots at home, and Napoli without Rafa Marin may sit deep, but City's recent attacking play has been criticised as predictable. I stay with the estimate.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target and I lean slightly lower. Maresca has said City cannot rely only on Haaland for goals, which hints at a lack of clear chances elsewhere. Napoli scored only once in Porto, so their share of efforts on target should be small.
